notes: SOURCE (all NARRATOR, second person, the town speaking): Level 200 is 'Home' and has always been around; a small, unremarkable town of about 4,000 people you will come to know; a smell of burning rust in your ears and the faint sound of skin breaking from the sky; the visitor arrives exhausted, clothes torn, barely fed; 'Let's take a walk'; Joe Vee has run the breakfast place for 60 years and has held the same soup bowl for 30 days, and it is starting to fall apart; the school could become your school as you remember it; space camp in the science lab, Sarah Palmer's dare to go into the dark, cold basement ('Below, below, below'), you might have believed you were falling apart down there; 'Bring her with you'; rot that only grows when you notice it AND only grows when you are not around (both kept); the house that used to be beautiful, chipped paint, walls grown too thin, not taken shape yet, and the request to remember walks with Mother, birthdays, and not thinking about living and dying; residents getting old, Ms. Garcia will bisect if you look too hard; 'This town needs new blood', 'Stay', 'Look behind you. Everyone's here.'; exits deflected. The licence box credits a photo of a small-town Main Street, which sets the architecture. ADAPTATION: one block of Main Street (frame houses north, storefronts, the diner and the school south) closed at both ends by a T-junction where the townspeople stand shoulder to shoulder across the road, with walking slowing to a crawl as you approach (the street never ends in a world edge; depth fog from 16 to 95 m, back fences, hedges); overcast 'bleak blue sky' daylight (from the remembered mornings; the present time of day is not stated); the house plan (10 x 9 m, two storeys, 16-riser stair of 0.1875 m, open gallery, porch with three steps; no basement or attic because the page gives the house neither); three memory groups (walks: hall, living room, den; birthday: dining room, kitchen; childhood: bedrooms, bathroom) whose walls/fabrics/lights lerp from chipped, stained, colourless and cold to whole and warm; the spare room never takes shape (bare studs); rot rates (0.06/s while in view within 11 m, 0.0025/s while you are in another zone; remembering cuts it to 30 percent, never zero; heavy rot greys a remembered group again); Ms. Garcia comes apart after about 6 s of direct looking (non-gory: two halves lean apart along a dark seam); Joe's bowl loses a shard every 50 s or when you look at it; the school basement memory ('Remember the dare') makes Sarah Palmer appear, back turned, at the house's landing window; after all three memories the narrator closes ('stay ... look behind you') and up to nine static residents are placed behind the player; the birthday card and report card are invented in-world props (names deliberately blank). Neither 4,000 residents nor 'you will know them all' is simulated beyond the crowds. Smell is a caption only. Not built: Level 199/201 (link list only, no edges).
